rows.ARS:
Dark red Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: MEIcauf
Exhibition name: Amalia ™
rows.Origin:
Bred by Alain Meilland (1940-....) (France, 1985).
Introduced in France by Meilland et Cie in 1989 as 'Amalia'.
Introduced in United States by Conard-Pyle (Star Roses) in 1990 as 'Amalia'.
rows.Bloom: Dark red. Strong fragrance. 40 petals. Average diameter 5". Large, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Armed with thorns / prickles. Medium, semi-glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: 39" to 5' (100 to 150cm). Width: 3' to 4' (90 to 120cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b and warmer. Can be used for container rose, cut flower or garden. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
